name: options-roots-b
prompt: Output ONE image, 16:9. A contact sheet of FOUR separate paintings in a 2 by 2 grid, each the same size, separated by thin plain dark gutters; no labels, no letters, no numbers, no text anywhere. Each painting is a different concept for the same view: the inside of one terrarium room, edge to edge (no case, no frame, no box edges), seen straight on from a low eye height, wide, the back softly out of focus and the ground sharp. Each is a small ROOT-AND-BURROW room, composed like a fine naturalistic vivarium: a TRIANGULAR composition, HIGH at the LEFT and low at the right: a mossy mound with an old root tangle rising at the left, and in it a dark round BURROW MOUTH at about a third of the width, the strongest point of the picture; the planting rising in levels from the front to the back; the right side low and open, with a soft calm mossy hollow at the lower right (from about 77 to 96 percent of the width, the bottom tenth of the height) where small creatures sleep, nothing standing in it. THE GROUND: a living, CALM ground of moss and fine soil in large soft patches, low in contrast, nothing scattered on it (no pebbles, no twigs, no succulents), so small dark, brown and teal creatures read clearly. One RAISED level: the lower flank of the mound at the left forms a low mossy terrace with a flat walkable top, joined to the main ground by a gentle mossy ramp. NO fittings at all: no pipes, no hoses, no misters, no vents, no lamps, no objects; no small pieces at the front. Painted in a hand-crafted miniature-diorama finish: fine painterly grain, soft bokeh behind; never photographic, never toon, never childish, no cartoon outlines, no toy colours, no gloss, no glow. No creatures, no animals, no figures. The four concepts must be clearly different in palette, mood and light. EVERY painting is welcoming, bright and alive, never spooky, never gloomy, never dark; NO gold, NO amber, NO honey or orange light (that is another room), NO deep dark fern green (that is another room). The tree is SMALL: only a slender trunk's base and its roots, the burrow mouth about an eighth of the picture's height, so the room reads at the scale of small creatures. TOP LEFT: a BLUEBELL CARPET: drifts of blue-violet bluebells behind the ground's back edge under pale silver-grey beech roots, fresh spring-green leaves above, soft bright morning light; the ground calm moss. TOP RIGHT: a SPRING WILDFLOWER BANK: small white and pink wildflowers (wood anemones, campion) on the mound and behind the ground, fresh lime-green moss, light grey-brown roots, clear bright light. BOTTOM LEFT: a SUNNY DEWY MORNING: clear cool light from the upper left, dew sparkling on lime and sage moss, pale grey-brown roots, a bright pale blue-green airy back. BOTTOM RIGHT: a SILVER BIRCH BANK at noon: white-and-grey birch roots and a slim white trunk base, fresh light-green young leaves, a few violets and white stitchwort behind the ground, crisp clear daylight.
